used_by: Next.js home route, shown when the site opens

sections.name: File setup, Tab
sections.title: Imports and tab type
sections.what: Brings in the page pieces and icons, and defines the two tab names the page accepts.
sections.why: Likely reason: limiting tab names to two stops a typo from creating an extra tab.

sections.name: Home
sections.title: Main page layout and tab switching
sections.what: Draws the header, the two tab buttons and the active section. Records each successfully indexed collection so the query section can offer it.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared list in the page lets both sections use the same collection names.
sections.watch_out: Only the active tab is drawn, so the other tab's typed text and results disappear from the screen.

summary: The main page: shows a header and two tabs, Index Documents and Ask Questions, and remembers which collections were indexed in this visit.
purpose: Lets the owner switch between loading documents and asking questions on one page.
why: Likely reason: keeps the two main features together, with a tab switch between them.
how: Starts with the index tab open and an empty collection list. When indexing succeeds, adds that collection name to the list. Draws the header, the two tab buttons, and the section for the active tab. The query section receives the collection list.
inputs: Tab button clicks and the success call from the index section.
outputs: The visible tab and the collection list passed to the query section.
risks: The collection list is kept only in memory, so a page refresh clears it. Switching tabs removes the other section from the screen, which can lose a typed question or answer.
debug: If a collection is missing from the question dropdown, check whether the page was refreshed after indexing. If a typed question disappears after switching tabs, that is how this page is built.
